sections.subtitle: Prva epizoda Redefinicije: gost s austrijskim prezimenom i ljubavlju prema jeziku
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel Wurzberg objašnjava porijeklo svojeg prezimena i obiteljsku pozadinu
sections.content:
Podcast **Redefinicija** novi je projekt portala **Muževni budite**. Voditelj Kruno otvara ga pozdravom „Hvaljen Isus i Marija, i sveti Josip” i najavljuje da će se u emisiji govoriti o muževnosti, očinstvu, liderstvu, poduzetništvu i drugim muškim temama.

Prvi gost je **Daniel Wurzberg**. Voditelj ga predstavlja kao oca četvero djece, supruga jedne žene i člana udruge Fokus. Kroz udrugu Daniel provodi projekte koji muškarcima pomažu da odbace pasivnost, preuzmu odgovornost i otkriju svrhu svojeg života. Kruno ističe da smatra velikim blagoslovom što baš on otvara prvu epizodu.

Prije ozbiljnih tema voditelj, i sam germanist, pita Daniela odakle mu prezime koje mnogi ne znaju izgovoriti. Daniel objašnjava da je rođen u Zagrebu, a djed u Slavonskom Brodu. Pradjed je rođen u **Austriji**, pa obitelj potječe iz vremena austro-ugarskog naseljavanja ovih krajeva. Pradjed se oženio Poljakinjom rođenom u **Ukrajini**. Obitelj se najprije nastanila u **Bosni**, u okolici **Banje Luke**, a zatim prešla preko **Save**. Daniel se kroz šalu opisuje kao „čistokrvnog” baš kao prosječan Hrvat, a Kruno to sažima kao „multikulti slučaj”.

Voditelj podsjeća i na Danielovo obrazovanje. Završio je **lingvistiku i informacijske znanosti**. Daniel priznaje da je planirao upisati samo informacijske znanosti, a lingvistiku je upisao gotovo slučajno. Taj mu se studij jako svidio jer je oduvijek volio sistematski pristup jeziku. Kaže da nije poliglot, a lingvistika mu je danas ostala na razini hobija: istražuje, čita tekstove i proučava jezik.
sections.subtitle_en: The first episode of Redefinicija: a guest with an Austrian surname and a love for language
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel Wurzberg explains the origin of his surname and his family background
sections.content_en:
The podcast **Redefinicija** is a new project of the portal **Muževni budite**. The host Kruno opens it with the greeting “Praised be Jesus and Mary, and Saint Joseph” and announces that the show will discuss masculinity, fatherhood, leadership, entrepreneurship, and other men's topics.

The first guest is **Daniel Wurzberg**. The host introduces him as a father of four children, husband of one wife, and a member of the association udruga Fokus. Through the association, Daniel conducts projects that help men reject passivity, assume responsibility, and discover the purpose of their life. Kruno emphasizes that he considers it a great blessing that he specifically opens the first episode.

Before the serious topics, the host, himself a Germanist, asks Daniel where his surname comes from, which many do not know how to pronounce. Daniel explains that he was born in Zagreb, and his grandfather in Slavonski Brod. His great-grandfather was born in **Austria**, so the family originates from the time of the Austro-Hungarian settlement of these parts. His great-grandfather married a Polish woman born in **Ukraine**. The family first settled in **Bosnia**, in the vicinity of **Banja Luka**, and then crossed over the **Sava**. Daniel jokingly describes himself as “purebred” just like an average Croat, and Kruno summarizes this as a “multi-culti case”.

The host also recalls Daniel's education. He graduated in **linguistics and information sciences**. Daniel admits that he had planned to enroll only in information sciences, and enrolled in linguistics almost by chance. He really liked that study because he had always loved a systematic approach to language. He says that he is not a polyglot, and linguistics has remained at the level of a hobby for him today: he researches, reads texts, and studies language.

sections.subtitle: Trideset godina Fokusa: od studenata ratnih godina do programa za obitelji
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel Wurzberg govori o povijesti udruge Fokus i programu Fokus obitelj
sections.content:
Daniel je u udruzi **Fokus** zaposlen puno radno vrijeme već 13 godina. Udruga je prošle godine proslavila **30 godina djelovanja u Hrvatskoj**. Nastala je u ratnim godinama, a u početku se bavila studentima, odnosno sljedećom generacijom vođa. Postupno su se razvijali i drugi programi. Krajem devedesetih pokrenut je program koji danas nosi ime **Fokus obitelj**, a usmjeren je na bračne parove i obitelji.

Tom su se dijelu rada Daniel i njegova supruga **Kate** priključili prije 13 godina. Sedam su godina volontirali u različitim programima i ulogama. Kako Daniel slikovito kaže, njihov „fokus unutar Fokusa” uvijek su bili bračni parovi i obitelji.

**Kako se živi od providnosti**

Kruno primjećuje da se mnogi čude kad čuju da netko radi u udruzi i pitaju od čega takvi ljudi žive. Prisjeća se da mu je upravo Daniel, prije nego što je pokrenuo vlastitu udrugu, dao poticaj koji mu je bio velik vjetar u leđa: **Bog uvijek plaća projekte koje On naručuje**.

Daniel objašnjava da se Fokus, kao i većina neprofitnih udruga, financira donacijama ljudi koji cijene njihov rad. To su uglavnom pojedinci, parovi i obitelji koji žele vidjeti promjenu u društvu. Programi nisu zamišljeni da donose profit i udruga ne prodaje proizvode. Cilj je pomoći ljudima da otkriju poruku evanđelja Isusa Krista i primijene je u razdoblju života u kojem se nalaze. Student, primjerice, ne treba čekati budućnost, nego već na fakultetu može biti koristan član zajednice. Mnogi parovi s vremenom prepoznaju vrijednost koju su primili pa se odluče za mjesečne donacije.

Daniel ne skriva da rad u neprofitnom sektoru zna biti obeshrabrujuć. Ljudima često ponestane sredstava i tada više ne mogu raditi ono što žele. U Fokusu su dobili dobru obuku o prikupljanju sredstava i predstavljanju svojeg rada. Uz to čvrsto vjeruju da je taj rad Božji poziv, barem za ovo razdoblje njihova života. To daje težinu i njihovu pozivu na donacije, jer ljudi vide da to ne rade samo kao posao. Donacije Daniel vidi i kao svojevrsni **„Božji korektivni faktor”**. Ako jednom presuše, protumačit će to kao znak da je vrijeme za nešto drugo. Kruno to sažima mišlju da će tada svoje poslanje smatrati ispunjenim.
sections.subtitle_en: Thirty years of Fokus: from students of the war years to programs for families
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel Wurzberg talks about the history of the Fokus association and the Fokus obitelj program
sections.content_en:
Daniel has been employed full-time in the **Fokus** association for 13 years already. Last year, the association celebrated **30 years of activity in Croatia**. It was formed during the war years, and in the beginning it dealt with students, that is, the next generation of leaders. Gradually, other programs also developed. At the end of the nineties, a program was launched that today bears the name **Fokus obitelj**, and is directed toward married couples and families.

Daniel and his wife **Kate** joined that part of the work 13 years ago. For seven years they volunteered in various programs and roles. As Daniel picturesquely says, their "focus within Fokus" was always married couples and families.

**How one lives on providence**

Kruno notes that many wonder when they hear that someone works in an association and ask what such people live on. He recalls that it was Daniel who, before he started his own association, gave him an encouragement that was a great tailwind for him: **God always pays for the projects that He orders**.

Daniel explains that Fokus, like most non-profit associations, is funded by donations from people who appreciate their work. These are mostly individuals, couples, and families who want to see change in society. The programs are not designed to generate profit and the association does not sell products. The goal is to help people discover the message of the Gospel of Jesus Christ and apply it in the period of life they are in. A student, for example, does not need to wait for the future, but already in college can be a useful member of the community. Many couples over time recognize the value they have received, so they decide on monthly donations.

Daniel does not hide that work in the non-profit sector can be discouraging. People often run out of funds and then can no longer do what they want. In Fokus, they received good training on fundraising and presenting their work. In addition, they firmly believe that this work is God's calling, at least for this period of their life. This gives weight also to their call for donations, because people see that they do not do it just as a job. Daniel also sees donations as a kind of **"God's corrective factor"**. If they dry up one day, he will interpret that as a sign that it is time for something else. Kruno summarizes this with the thought that they will then consider their mission fulfilled.

sections.subtitle: Iz osobne potrebe do poziva: edukatori, a ne terapeuti
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel objašnjava zašto se on i Kate smatraju edukatorima, a ne terapeutima
sections.content:
Kruno pita kako su Daniel i Kate prepoznali da ih Bog zove u predbračno i bračno savjetovanje. Daniel odgovara da je sve počelo iz njihove **osobne potrebe**. Kao volonteri postupno su dobivali sve više odgovornosti. Najprije su vodili male grupe za bračne parove, a zatim su ih pozivali da govore na konferencijama.

Nakon nekoliko godina sazrelo je u njima čvrsto uvjerenje. Željeli su drugima biti ono što su njihovom braku bili ljudi koji su im služili. Tada su prvi put ozbiljno razmišljali o punovremenoj službi i zaposlenju u Fokusu.

Ove su godine Daniel i Kate obilježili **20 godina braka**. Daniel naglašava da im i danas trebaju utjecaj drugih zdravih brakova i male grupe. Svaka priprema za predavanje prilika je da preispitaju vlastiti odnos, kako drugima ne bi govorili ono što sami ne žive. Etiketa stručnjaka uvijek je izazov, pa ljudima rado kažu da nisu stručni ni u čemu, osim u tome da su više puta pogriješili i ponekad pronašli dobro rješenje.

Sebe zato vide prije svega kao **edukatore**. Neki njihovi dugogodišnji kolege stekli su diplome iz bračnog i obiteljskog savjetovanja. Daniel i Kate se ipak ne vide u psihoterapijskom pristupu u kojem bi savjetovanje bilo glavni dio posla. Savjetovanja vode koliko mogu, ali najveći napredak vide u **malim grupama**, gdje se par stalno izlaže dobrim sadržajima.
sections.subtitle_en: From personal need to a calling: educators, not therapists
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel explains why he and Kate consider themselves educators, not therapists
sections.content_en:
Kruno asks how Daniel and Kate recognized that God was calling them into premarital and marriage counseling. Daniel replies that everything started from their **personal need**. As volunteers, they gradually received more and more responsibility. First they led small groups for married couples, and then they were invited to speak at conferences.

After several years, a firm conviction matured in them. They wanted to be to others what the people who served them had been to their marriage. That was when they first seriously considered full-time ministry and employment at Fokus.

This year Daniel and Kate marked **20 years of marriage**. Daniel emphasizes that even today they need the influence of other healthy marriages and small groups. Every preparation for a lecture is an opportunity to re-examine their own relationship, so that they would not speak to others what they do not live themselves. The label of expert is always a challenge, so they gladly tell people that they are not experts in anything, except in having made mistakes multiple times and sometimes finding a good solution.

That is why they see themselves primarily as **educators**. Some of their long-time colleagues earned degrees in marriage and family counseling. Daniel and Kate, however, do not see themselves in a psychotherapeutic approach in which counseling would be the main part of the work. They conduct counseling as much as they can, but they see the greatest progress in **small groups**, where a couple is constantly exposed to good content.

sections.subtitle: Brak kao automobil: zašto parovima treba šest godina da zatraže pomoć
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel prepričava primjer para pred razvodom kojem je pomoglo pravilo olovke
sections.content:
Voditelj otvara pitanje otpora prema savjetovanju. Mnogi parovi misle da je ono rezervirano za veze pri kraju, boje se što će drugi misliti ili pomoć doživljavaju kao poraz. Zato probleme rješavaju sami ili se žale bližnjima, koji stvar često samo dodatno napuhnu.

Daniel se slaže da u društvu postoji velika **stigma**. Paradoks je u tome što svi oko para već znaju da imaju ozbiljnih problema, a njima je i dalje teško potražiti stručnu pomoć. Kod automobila takvih dvojbi nema. Prije deset godina čovjek je možda mogao sam popraviti auto, a moderni automobili traže ozbiljnog mehaničara. Nitko se ne srami platiti, otići na servis i reći da nešto ne zna, jer želi da mu auto dobro služi. Brak, nasuprot tome, mnogi doživljavaju kao da je dan vjenčanja vrhunac. Daniel ističe da je to zapravo tek **„day one”**. Prenosi i misao da bi parovi bili u puno boljoj situaciji kad bi u brak uložili koliko su potrošili na svadbu.

**Mit o kriznoj sedmoj godini**

Daniel spominje jedno američko istraživanje. Prema njemu je sedma godina krizna zato što parovima obično treba šest godina da priznaju kako im treba ozbiljna pomoć. U tome nema ničeg čarobnog, samo svi odugovlače i misle da će proći. Usput se povjeravaju najboljem prijatelju, susjedi, kumi ili roditeljima.

Iz iskustva Daniel zaključuje da većina problema nisu nepremostive krize, nego **nedostatak vještina rješavanja sukoba i zdrave komunikacije**. Te se vještine mogu naučiti, ali za to treba potražiti nekoga tko ih može prenijeti. Najbolji prijatelj, primjećuje Daniel, najčešće je u istoj situaciji, samo se taj tjedan još nije posvađao.

**Pravilo olovke**

Pomak ponekad dođe vrlo brzo. Daniel opisuje par koji je bio gotovo pred razvodom. Objasnili su im pravilo prema kojem pravo govora ima samo onaj tko drži olovku, žlicu ili neki drugi predmet. Kad su to prvi put isprobali na kauču pred Danielom i Kate, napokon su se čuli bez upadanja u riječ i prekidanja. Njima je to bilo nevjerojatno, a Daniel i Kate su se smijali koliko je ideja s kemijskom jednostavna. Daniel upozorava da to nije rješenje za sve, nego **prva pomoć za hitne situacije**.

Poruka mu je da u svaki odnos treba ulagati, kao u sport ili u tim. Parove potiče da se uključe u programe koji obogaćuju brak, ne zato što je zadnji trenutak, nego zato što žele da brak dugo traje. Autu se svake godine mijenja ulje, a nemar na kraju košta više. Odnosi vrijede više od svega što se može kupiti novcem. Kad par ima djecu, šteta se prenosi i na sljedeću generaciju i zna biti ogromna.
sections.subtitle_en: Marriage like a car: why it takes couples six years to seek help
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel recounts an example of a couple on the verge of divorce who were helped by the pencil rule
sections.content_en:
The host opens the question of resistance toward counseling. Many couples think that it is reserved for relationships near their end, fear what others will think, or perceive help as defeat. Therefore, they solve problems on their own or complain to those close to them, who often only blow the matter further out of proportion.

Daniel agrees that there is a great **stigma** in society. The paradox is that everyone around the couple already knows that they have serious problems, yet it is still difficult for them to seek professional help. With cars, there are no such doubts. Ten years ago, a person might have been able to fix a car by himself, while modern cars require a serious mechanic. No one is ashamed to pay, go to a service shop, and say that they do not know something, because they want their car to serve them well. Marriage, by contrast, many perceive as if the wedding day were the culmination. Daniel points out that this is actually only **„day one”**. He also conveys the thought that couples would be in a much better situation if they invested into marriage as much as they spent on the wedding.

**The myth of the crisis seventh year**

Daniel mentions an American study. According to it, the seventh year is critical because it usually takes couples six years to admit that they need serious help. There is nothing magical in that, it is just that everyone procrastinates and thinks that it will pass. Along the way, they confide in a best friend, a neighbor, a godmother, or parents.

From experience, Daniel concludes that most problems are not insurmountable crises, but rather a **lack of conflict resolution skills and healthy communication**. These skills can be learned, but for that, one must seek someone who can pass them on. The best friend, Daniel observes, is most often in the same situation, only that week they haven't had an argument yet.

**The pencil rule**

Progress sometimes comes very quickly. Daniel describes a couple who were almost on the verge of divorce. They explained to them the rule according to which only the one holding a pencil, a spoon, or some other object has the right to speak. When they tested this for the first time on the couch in front of Daniel and Kate, they finally heard each other without interrupting and cutting each other off. To them it was incredible, while Daniel and Kate laughed at how simple the idea with the pen was. Daniel warns that this is not a solution for everything, but rather **first aid for emergency situations**.

His message is that one must invest in every relationship, like in sports or in a team. He encourages couples to get involved in programs that enrich marriage, not because it is the last moment, but because they want the marriage to last a long time. A car's oil is changed every year, and neglect ends up costing more. Relationships are worth more than anything that can be bought with money. When a couple has children, the damage is passed on to the next generation as well and can be enormous.

sections.subtitle: Ulaganje prije prvog dana: zašto jedno predavanje vikendom nije dovoljno
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel opisuje zaručnički tečaj od sedam susreta koji provodi Fokus
sections.content:
Kruno pita isplati li se u brak ulagati i prije njegova početka, za vrijeme zaruka. Navodi da poznaje mnoge parove kojima je predbračno savjetovanje pomoglo i spriječilo da se problemi u braku umnože.

Daniel odgovara potvrdno i poziva se na vlastito iskustvo. Iako su on i Kate mislili da se dobro poznaju, tečaj je otvorio teme o kojima nisu razgovarali ili koje im više nisu bile na radaru. Zato potiče mlade da odaberu **dobar predbračni tečaj**. Neki su mu se požalili da se tečaj kod njih svodi na jedno ili dva predavanja tijekom vikenda. Daniel smatra da je to premalo, jer se u tako kratkom vremenu ne mogu ni otvoriti vlastita pitanja i nedoumice.

Zaručnički tečaj koji vode Daniel i Kate ima **šest plus jedan, odnosno sedam susreta**, i traje dva do tri mjeseca. U tom razmaku par stigne dublje promisliti o pitanjima, pa i posvađati se, te otkriti što ga zaista žulja i o čemu još treba razgovarati.

Najveća greška mladih je da tečaj odrade samo kako bi drugi vidjeli da su bili. Tako najmanje dobiju. Daniel ih poziva da tečaj shvate ozbiljno i daju si najbolju priliku da se pripreme. Ipak, naglašava da se za brak **nitko ne može do kraja pripremiti**. Sudbonosno „da, uzimam” potpuno preobražava dvije osobe i stvara nešto novo, iako osobnosti i povijesti ostaju iste. Ono što se može učiniti jest što bolje upoznati sebe i drugu osobu: što voli, što preferira i kakvu **prtljagu** nosi iz obitelji, vrijednosti i odgoja. Duži tečaj daje prostor da se ta prtljaga raspakira.
sections.subtitle_en: Investing before day one: why one weekend lecture is not enough
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel describes the seven-meeting marriage preparation course conducted by Fokus
sections.content_en:
Kruno asks whether it pays off to invest in marriage even before its beginning, during the engagement. He states that he knows many couples whom premarital counseling helped and prevented problems in marriage from multiplying.

Daniel answers affirmatively and refers to his own experience. Although he and Kate thought they knew each other well, the course opened up topics they had not talked about or that were no longer on their radar. That is why he encourages young people to choose a **good premarital course**. Some have complained to him that where they are, the course comes down to one or two lectures over a weekend. Daniel considers that to be too little, because in such a short time one cannot even open one's own questions and doubts.

The marriage preparation course led by Daniel and Kate has **six plus one, that is, seven meetings**, and lasts two to three months. In that span, a couple has time to reflect more deeply on questions, and even have an argument, and discover what truly bothers them and what still needs to be talked about.

The biggest mistake of young people is doing the course just so others can see that they attended. That way they get the least. Daniel invites them to take the course seriously and give themselves the best opportunity to prepare. Nevertheless, he emphasizes that **no one can fully prepare** for marriage. The fateful “yes, I do” completely transforms two people and creates something new, although personalities and histories remain the same. What can be done is to get to know oneself and the other person as well as possible: what they love, what they prefer, and what kind of **baggage** they carry from family, values, and upbringing. A longer course provides the space for that baggage to be unpacked.

sections.subtitle: Ubojice veze i trik s kaučem: nismo mi problem, problem je naš
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel pokazuje razliku između sjedenja licem u lice i gledanja u istom smjeru
sections.content:
Kruno pita koje su najčešće „ubojice” veze i braka. Daniel odgovara da se parovi, bez obzira na temu, najviše svađaju zbog **nedostatka dobre i kvalitetne komunikacije**. Previše čitaju između redova, pretpostavljaju umjesto da provjere i nose razočarana očekivanja koja se nisu ispunila jer nisu bila jasno izrečena. Često nije presudno što je problem, nego **kako mu se pristupilo** i jesu li partneri mogli dobro razgovarati.

**Gledati u istom smjeru**

Daniel prenosi savjet koji su on i Kate nedavno isprobali na jednom programu, gdje su više sudjelovali nego moderirali. Kad pred parom stoji težak razgovor, partneri ne bi trebali sjediti jedan nasuprot drugome, kao Daniel i Kruno u studiju. Bolje je sjesti na kauč i okrenuti se u istom smjeru. Govor tijela tada poručuje: *nisam protiv tebe, nego zajedno gledamo u naš problem i tražimo rješenje.* Bilo da je riječ o novcu, djeci ili roditeljima, par tako lakše vidi da je problem zajednički, a da oni sami nisu problem.

Daniel i Kate kod kuće često idu u **šetnju** kad trebaju razgovarati o nekom problemu. Šetnja ih prisiljava da oboje gledaju naprijed, razgovaraju i mole. Nakon pola sata nisu sve riješili, ali su izbjegli međusobne napade i stalnu potrebu za obranom. Možda još nisu došli do zaključka, ali su se čuli, a to je prvi korak.

Na Krunovu šalu o deset tisuća koraka Daniel odgovara da ih je prije pet tisuća. Dodaje da takva šetnja znači i zajedničko vrijeme i svjež zrak, kao i svjesnu odluku da se radi na odnosu. Priznaje da je sklon guranju stvari pod tepih. Šetnja ga primora da progovori, jer zna zašto su izašli i ne može samo šutjeti. Tako oboje dobivaju **fer podlogu** da se čuju i dobro razgovaraju.
sections.subtitle_en: Relationship killers and the couch trick: we are not the problem, the problem is ours
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel shows the difference between sitting face to face and looking in the same direction
sections.content_en:
Kruno asks what are the most common “killers” of a relationship and marriage. Daniel answers that couples, regardless of the topic, argue the most because of **a lack of good and quality communication**. They read too much between the lines, assume instead of checking, and carry disappointed expectations that were not fulfilled because they were not clearly stated. Often it is not crucial what the problem is, but **how it was approached** and whether the partners were able to talk well.

**Looking in the same direction**

Daniel shares advice that he and Kate recently tried out at a program where they participated more than they moderated. When a couple faces a difficult conversation, the partners should not sit opposite each other, like Daniel and Kruno in the studio. It is better to sit on the couch and face in the same direction. Body language then communicates: *I am not against you, but together we look at our problem and seek a solution.* Whether it is about money, children, or parents, it is easier for the couple to see that the problem is shared, and that they themselves are not the problem.

At home, Daniel and Kate often go for a **walk** when they need to talk about a problem. The walk forces them both to look forward, talk, and pray. After half an hour, they have not resolved everything, but they have avoided mutual attacks and the constant need for defense. Perhaps they have not yet reached a conclusion, but they heard each other, and that is the first step.

To Kruno's joke about ten thousand steps, Daniel replies that it is more like five thousand. He adds that such a walk means both time together and fresh air, as well as a conscious decision to work on the relationship. He admits that he is prone to sweeping things under the rug. The walk forces him to speak up, because he knows why they went out and he cannot just remain silent. In this way, both get a **fair foundation** to hear each other and have a good conversation.

sections.subtitle: Slušati da bi razumio, a ne da bi odgovorio: „kako to” umjesto „zašto”
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel objašnjava zašto pitanje „zašto” izaziva obranu, a „kako to” otvara razgovor
sections.content:
Kruno traži konkretne savjete za bolju komunikaciju. Daniel kaže da se svi savjeti svode na jednostavne korake, ali da je ključna **unutarnja motivacija** da se čovjek time želi baviti. Glavna su načela da partneri čuju jedno drugo, da se ne prekidaju i ne upadaju si u riječ.

**Slušanje kao obavijest o tuđim manama**

Najveća lekcija, prema Danielu, glasi: **slušati da bi razumio**. Priznaje da u svađi sluša da bi odgovorio. Dok mu Kate govori, on već smišlja obranu. Tada ne sudjeluje u komunikaciji, nego ima „obavijest” za nju: ona ga informira o njegovim manama, a on će nju o njezinima. Tako se ne riješi ništa.

Daniel preporučuje knjige, tečajeve i seminare o komunikaciji. Komunikaciju vidi kao **vještinu koja se razvija**. Nekima ide prirodno, a njemu teže. Cilj nije savršenstvo, nego napredak: tko je na ljestvici od jedan do deset na dvojci, može se truditi doći do trojke.

**Ja-izjave i čarolija dviju riječi**

Među malim pomacima Daniel ističe izjave koje počinju s „ja”, a ne s „ti”, kako bi se izbjeglo optuživanje. Posebno izdvaja jednostavan savjet. Kad partner želi doznati zašto se nešto dogodilo ili nije dogodilo, neka pitanje ne počne sa „zašto”, nego s **„kako to”**. Na pitanje „zašto si kasnio?” prva je reakcija opravdavanje. Na pitanje „kako to da si kasnio?” lako je odgovoriti da je bio sudar ili da nije bilo parkinga, pa razgovor ostaje prijateljski.

Daniel priznaje da i sam pitanje sa „zašto” doživljava kao napad, što Kruno odmah prepoznaje. Tada se gradi zid, a razgovor postaje ping-pong izjava. Ono što jedan kaže drugi doživljava kao izvlačenje i nepreuzimanje odgovornosti. Zato Daniel i sam mora vježbati. Umjesto da pretpostavi da je Kate imala vremena, pita je kako to da nije skuhala ručak. Ona odgovori da ju je netko nazvao i da je morala biti s djecom, i to mu je potpuno u redu.

**Znatiželja umjesto osude**

Ako su partneri **znatiželjni, a ne osuđujući**, odnos trpi puno manje pritiska. Daniel naglašava da su on i Kate dvoje ljudi koji su se odabrali s dobrim namjerama. Pogreške se događaju, ali partneri jedan drugome čuvaju leđa time što **vjeruju u najbolje kod drugoga**.
sections.subtitle_en: Listening to understand, not to respond: "how come" instead of "why"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel explains why the question "why" triggers defensiveness, while "how come" opens up conversation
sections.content_en:
Kruno asks for concrete advice for better communication. Daniel says that all advice comes down to simple steps, but that the key is **inner motivation** that one wants to deal with it. The main principles are that partners hear each other, that they do not interrupt each other and do not cut each other off.

**Listening as a notification about someone else's flaws**

The greatest lesson, according to Daniel, is: **listening to understand**. He admits that in an argument he listens to respond. While Kate speaks to him, he is already devising a defense. Then he is not participating in communication, but has a "notice" for her: she informs him about his flaws, and he will inform her about hers. That way, nothing gets resolved.

Daniel recommends books, courses, and seminars on communication. He sees communication as a **skill that is developed**. For some it comes naturally, and for him it is harder. The goal is not perfection, but progress: whoever is at a two on a scale from one to ten can strive to reach a three.

**I-statements and the magic of two words**

Among the small shifts, Daniel highlights statements that begin with "I", and not with "you", in order to avoid blaming. He especially singles out a simple piece of advice. When a partner wants to find out why something happened or did not happen, let the question not begin with "why", but with **"how come"**. To the question "why were you late?" the first reaction is making excuses. To the question "how come you were late?" it is easy to answer that there was a car accident or that there was no parking, so the conversation remains friendly.

Daniel admits that he himself experiences a question with "why" as an attack, which Kruno immediately recognizes. Then a wall is built, and the conversation becomes a ping-pong of statements. What one says, the other perceives as making excuses and not taking responsibility. That is why Daniel himself must practice. Instead of assuming that Kate had time, he asks her how come she did not cook lunch. She answers that someone called her and that she had to be with the children, and that is completely fine with him.

**Curiosity instead of judgment**

If partners are **curious and not judgmental**, the relationship suffers much less pressure. Daniel emphasizes that he and Kate are two people who chose each other with good intentions. Mistakes happen, but partners have each other's back by **believing the best in the other**.

sections.subtitle: Fizičkost kao zamagljene naočale: zašto dodir ne vrijedi tisuću riječi
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel uspoređuje fizičku intimnost s naočalama koje se zamagle pri otvaranju pećnice
sections.content:
Kruno primjećuje da neki parovi svađe rješavaju fizičkom intimnošću. Kad u braku nestane komunikacije, nestane i intimnosti na kojoj su gradili odnos. Pita kako Daniel gleda na intimne potrebe muškarca i žene, uz opasku da je muškarcima to visoko na ljestvici prioriteta, a žene to drukčije doživljavaju.

Daniel kaže da pitanje nije jednostavno. Upozorava na generalizaciju prema kojoj je muškarcima seksualna intimnost bitnija, a ženama nije. Prema njemu, to nije sasvim točno: ženama je jednako važna, samo do nje dolaze **drugim putem**.

**Zamagljivač u vezi**

Na zaručničkim tečajevima Daniel i Kate snažno savjetuju parovima da **„ohlade” od fizičkog**. Fizičkost smatraju jednim od najvećih **„zamagljivača”**, kako ga sami zovu. Daniel to uspoređuje s otvaranjem pećnice, kad se naočale potpuno zamagle. Fizički kontakt je komunikacija koja se odvija kroz tijelo: uzbuđenje, dodir, nježnost. Zbog toga lako nastaje **lažan dojam da se partneri razumiju**. Čini se dovoljnim zagrliti se i poljubiti, a par pritom postaje slijep za pravi problem i prestaje komunicirati. Daniel zaključuje da dodir ne vrijedi tisuću riječi. Svaki supružnik zna koliko toga u svađama ostane neizrečeno, a to se mora adekvatno riješiti.
sections.subtitle_en: Physicality as fogged-up glasses: why touch is not worth a thousand words
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel compares physical intimacy to glasses that fog up when opening the oven
sections.content_en:
Kruno notes that some couples resolve arguments with physical intimacy. When communication disappears in marriage, the intimacy on which they built the relationship also disappears. He asks how Daniel views the intimate needs of a man and a woman, noting that for men this is high on the list of priorities, while women experience it differently.

Daniel says that the question is not simple. He warns against the generalization according to which sexual intimacy is more important to men and not to women. According to him, that is not entirely true: it is just as important to women, they just reach it **by a different path**.

**The fogger in a relationship**

In marriage preparation courses, Daniel and Kate strongly advise couples to **"cool off" from the physical**. They consider physicality one of the greatest **"foggers"**, as they themselves call it. Daniel compares this to opening an oven, when glasses completely fog up. Physical contact is communication that takes place through the body: excitement, touch, tenderness. Because of this, a **false impression that the partners understand each other** easily arises. It seems enough to hug and kiss, while the couple becomes blind to the real problem and stops communicating. Daniel concludes that touch is not worth a thousand words. Every spouse knows how much remains unsaid in arguments, and that must be adequately resolved.

sections.subtitle: Istraživanje koje je iznenadilo: ženama najviše nedostaje muška inicijativa
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel prepričava istraživanje o glavnom razlogu manjka želje kod žena
sections.content:
Daniel spominje istraživanje predstavljeno na konferenciji na kojoj su on i Kate nedavno sudjelovali. Žene su u njemu kao **prvi razlog manjka želje za seksualnom intimnošću** navele **nedostatak muške inicijative**. Daniel priznaje da ga je to iznenadilo, jer je mislio da je to tipično muški odgovor. Muškarci, naime, često žele da žene više iniciraju.

Problem je, objašnjava Daniel, u tome što muškarci inicijativu shvaćaju samo u okviru bračne sobe. Ženama inicijativa znači nešto drugo:

- kako je muž pozdravi ujutro kad odlazi na posao,
- je li joj tijekom dana poslao poruku,
- kakve je volje kad se vrati s posla.

Sve to za ženu je inicijativa koja u njoj pokreće ono što želi pružiti mužu. Daniel ističe da žena svoju nutrinu procesuira kompleksnije od muškarca. Spominje video koji opisuje kao „Istina o dva mozga” ili nešto slično. U njemu je muški mozak prikazan kao niz zasebnih kutija, za posao, financije ili seksualnu intimnost, od kojih se svaka otvara posebno. Kod žene je sve isprepleteno, a Kruno dodaje da je sve povezano. Zato žena ne misli samo na to da muž nije inicirao navečer, nego na to da nije inicirao tijekom dana, da tjednima možda nisu razgovarali ni doživjeli trenutak stvarne povezanosti.
sections.subtitle_en: A study that surprised: women miss male initiative the most
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel recounts a study on the main reason for a lack of desire in women
sections.content_en:
Daniel mentions a study presented at a conference in which he and Kate recently participated. In it, as **the number one reason for the lack of desire for sexual intimacy**, women cited **the lack of male initiative**. Daniel admits that this surprised him, because he thought that was a typically male response. Men, namely, often want women to initiate more.

The problem, Daniel explains, is that men understand initiative only within the framework of the marital bedroom. To women, initiative means something else:

- how the husband greets her in the morning when he leaves for work,
- whether he sent her a message during the day,
- what kind of mood he is in when he returns from work.

All of that for a woman is initiative that triggers in her what she wants to give to her husband. Daniel emphasizes that a woman processes her inner world more complexly than a man. He mentions a video he describes as “The Truth About Two Brains” or something similar. In it, the male brain is depicted as a series of separate boxes, for work, finances, or sexual intimacy, each of which opens separately. With a woman, everything is intertwined, and Kruno adds that everything is connected. That is why a woman does not think only about the fact that the husband did not initiate in the evening, but about the fact that he did not initiate during the day, that for weeks they might not have talked or experienced a moment of genuine connection.

sections.subtitle: Dublja muška potreba: biti željen, voljen i stalno osvajati suprugu
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel opisuje trenutak kada je shvatio da je njegova potreba dublja od fizičke
sections.content:
Daniel otvoreno govori o vlastitom iskustvu. Kad su djeca bila mala, a supruga umorna i bez volje za bilo čim, pitao se je li normalno da on stalno ima želju, a ona gotovo nikad. Tada je shvatio da i njemu zapravo nedostaje **osjećaj da je željen, voljen i da pripada njoj**. Ne radi se samo o fizičkom činu kojim se „namiri” muškarac s velikom potrebom.

Daniel je uvidio da njegova potreba ide puno dublje. Iako se najčešće izražava kroz bračno zajedništvo, i on želi da ga se supruga sjeti, da mu pošalje poruku i da se veseli kad se vrati kući. Muškarci, zaključuje Daniel, sami sebe zavaravaju kad misle da bi bili sretniji kad bi samo bilo više intime. **Ispunjenje dolazi iz ispunjavajućeg odnosa** s osobom kojoj su rekli „da” zauvijek.

**Osvajanje ne prestaje vjenčanjem**

Muškarac ne može proizvesti ni kontrolirati volju i spremnost svoje supruge. Može je, međutim, **nastaviti osvajati**. Prije braka to je bilo prirodno: čokoladica, cvijet, šetnja parkom ili večera. Nakon osvajanja mnogi zaključe da je posao gotov. Kruno to slikovito opisuje izrekom da „zec više nije u šumi, zec je na ražnju”. Daniel se slaže i dodaje da su **žene stvorene da budu voljene**. Treba samo kreativno pronalaziti nove načine, a Kruno to sažima kao osvajanje iz dana u dan.
sections.subtitle_en: A deeper male need: to be desired, loved, and constantly winning over one's wife
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel describes the moment he realized his need was deeper than physical
sections.content_en:
Daniel speaks openly about his own experience. When the children were small, and his wife was tired and had no desire for anything, he wondered whether it was normal that he constantly had desire, while she almost never did. It was then that he realized that he too actually lacked **the feeling of being desired, loved, and belonging to her**. It is not merely about a physical act by which a man with a great need is "satisfied."

Daniel saw that his need goes much deeper. Although it is most often expressed through marital communion, he too wants his wife to remember him, to send him a message, and to be glad when he returns home. Men, Daniel concludes, deceive themselves when they think they would be happier if there were only more intimacy. **Fulfillment comes from a fulfilling relationship** with the person to whom they said "yes" forever.

**Winning her over does not end with marriage**

A man cannot produce or control his wife's will and readiness. He can, however, **continue to win her over**. Before marriage, that was natural: a chocolate bar, a flower, a walk in the park, or a dinner. After winning her over, many conclude that the job is done. Kruno vividly describes this with the saying that "the rabbit is no longer in the woods, the rabbit is on the spit." Daniel agrees and adds that **women are created to be loved**. One only needs to creatively find new ways, and Kruno summarizes this as winning her over from day to day.

sections.subtitle: Pornografija: ovisnost koja ne nestaje izgovorenim „da”
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel objašnjava da je pornografija ovisnost koja se prenosi u brak
sections.content:
Kruno pretpostavlja da muškarci zbog manjka bračne intimnosti bježe u pornografiju. Pita kako ona danas utječe na muškarce i čini li ih impotentnima ne samo spolno nego i emocionalno, socijalno i intelektualno.

Daniel se slaže s utjecajem, ali odmah ispravlja premisu. Pornografija, kaže, **nema veze s nedostatkom spolnosti u braku**. Većina muškaraca na nju se navikne mnogo prije nego što uopće pomisli na brak, a navika se zatim prenese i u brak. Mnogi naivno misle da je pornografija samo način nošenja sa stresom dok nemaju pristup bračnoj postelji. Zatim otkriju da i u braku jednako lako upadaju u njezine ralje.

Razlog je to što muškarac postaje **ovisan o pornografiji i zadovoljavanju požude**, a ne o spolnom činu. Tko je to radio deset ili petnaest godina prije braka, teško da će dan nakon vjenčanja reći da mu je to služilo samo da preživi. Daniel to smatra velikom zabludom. Zato je važno da se i mladi i stariji što prije uhvate u koštac s problemom i priznaju da imaju **ovisnost**. Što pornografija nije kazneno djelo ne znači da im ne treba ozbiljna pomoć.

**Impotentnost na svim razinama**

Daniel prati portale bez vjerskog ili moralnog stava o pornografiji. Na njima mladići s oduševljenjem pišu kako su nakon dva tjedna apstinencije puni ideja i uspješni na ispitima. Do tada su mislili da im pornografija čak i koristi. Sada otkrivaju svijet u kojem nisu zatupljeni ni prepušteni sami sebi i shvaćaju da bi u životu mogli nešto postići. Daniel zaključuje da je problem puno dublji od usputne teme. Upozorava i da se u vjerskim krugovima o pornografiji često govori samo moralistički, uz poruku da to ne bi trebalo. Svi znaju da je loša, ali se nitko ozbiljno ne uhvati u koštac s njom.
sections.subtitle_en: Pornography: an addiction that does not disappear with the spoken "I do"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel explains that pornography is an addiction that carries over into marriage
sections.content_en:
Kruno assumes that men escape into pornography because of a lack of marital intimacy. He asks how it affects men today and whether it makes them impotent not only sexually, but also emotionally, socially, and intellectually.

Daniel agrees with the impact, but immediately corrects the premise. Pornography, he says, **has nothing to do with the lack of sexuality in marriage**. Most men get used to it long before they even think about marriage, and the habit is then carried over into marriage. Many naively think that pornography is just a way of coping with stress while they do not have access to the marital bed. Then they discover that even in marriage they fall just as easily into its clutches.

The reason is that a man becomes **addicted to pornography and the satisfaction of lust**, not to the sexual act. Whoever has done that for ten or fifteen years before marriage will hardly say the day after the wedding that it only served him to survive. Daniel considers this a great delusion. That is why it is important that both young and older people tackle the problem as soon as possible and admit that they have an **addiction**. Just because pornography is not a criminal offense does not mean that they do not need serious help.

**Impotence on all levels**

Daniel follows portals without a religious or moral stance on pornography. On them, young men enthusiastically write about how, after two weeks of abstinence, they are full of ideas and successful on exams. Until then, they thought pornography was even beneficial to them. Now they discover a world in which they are neither dulled nor left to themselves, and they realize that they could achieve something in life. Daniel concludes that the problem is much deeper than a passing topic. He also warns that in religious circles pornography is often spoken of only moralistically, with the message that one shouldn't do that. Everyone knows that it is bad, but no one seriously tackles it.

sections.subtitle: Okidači, radikalni rezovi i Projekt 41: put iz ropstva
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel govori o radikalnim koracima koje muškarci moraju poduzeti da bi izašli iz ovisnosti
sections.content:
Daniel je kroz različite programe radio s muškarcima. Cilj nije bio samo da znaju kako je pornografija loša, nego da shvate **što ih do nje dovodi**: koji su im **okidači**, kad su najslabiji i u kojim joj se situacijama prepuštaju.

Ponekad su se morali dogovoriti o **radikalnim koracima**. Neki su morali ukinuti internet kod kuće ili promijeniti broj telefona kako im se ne bi javljale žene s kojima su ostvarivali ono na što ih je pornografija poticala. Tu se, kaže Daniel, vidi tko je stvarno ozbiljan. Nailazio je na otpor, primjerice na pitanje zašto bi netko mijenjao broj telefona. Daniel takvima odgovara da broj nije bitan. Tko ima dvadeset godina povijesti i nije uspio odrezati glavu toj zmiji, mora biti ekstremniji.

**Čistoća i u braku**

Kruno primjećuje da muškarci često vjeruju kako će potreba za pornografijom i samozadovoljavanjem nestati ulaskom u brak, a na kraju se prevare. Daniel dodaje da im ta **lažna nada** zapravo služi kao opravdanje. Uvjeravaju se da će prestati kad kažu „da”, kao da je to tako jednostavno. Upozorava i da se često govori samo o **predbračnoj čistoći**, kao da čistoća u braku nije potrebna. Neki se prije braka nisu upuštali u ono što ne bi trebali, a u braku nastave sa „svakakvim gadostima” s izgovorom da su se posvađali ili da nikome ne smeta ako nitko ne zna.

Daniel iznosi i osobno svjedočanstvo. Prve pornografske časopise počeo je listati s **10 ili 11 godina**, a oženio se s **24**. Takvom se sadržaju izlagao mnogo duže nego što je u prvom tjednu braka imao pristup bračnoj postelji. Zato nije realno očekivati da motivacija i stavovi preko noći nadvladaju dugogodišnje **ropstvo ovisnosti**. To treba shvatiti ozbiljno.

**Projekt 41**

Kruno navodi da danas postoji sve više programa za izlazak iz te ovisnosti. Njegova je udruga nedavno pokrenula **Projekt 41**, utemeljen na Svetom pismu i molitvi, namijenjen prije svega katoličkim muškarcima. Dolaze mu muškarci od 20 do 60 godina, u vezi ili u braku. Neki već imaju unučad, a gledaju pornografski sadržaj s djevojčicama dobi svojih unuka i ne mogu prestati. Kruno zaključuje da je to velika borba. Mogu se ponuditi svi alati, ali pomoći nema dok čovjek sam ne kaže: **„Dosta!”** Daniel se slaže.
sections.subtitle_en: Triggers, radical cuts, and Project 41: the way out of slavery
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel speaks about the radical steps men must take to get out of addiction
sections.content_en:
Through various programs, Daniel worked with men. The goal was not only for them to know that pornography is bad, but to understand **what leads them to it**: what their **triggers** are, when they are weakest, and in which situations they indulge in it.

Sometimes they had to agree on **radical steps**. Some had to cancel the internet at home or change their phone number so that women with whom they carried out what pornography prompted them to do would not contact them. That, says Daniel, is where one sees who is truly serious. He encountered resistance, for instance to the question of why someone would change their phone number. To such people, Daniel replies that the number is not important. Whoever has twenty years of history and has not managed to cut off that snake's head must be more extreme.

**Chastity in marriage as well**

Kruno notes that men often believe that the need for pornography and masturbation will disappear upon entering marriage, and in the end they are deceived. Daniel adds that this **false hope** actually serves as an excuse for them. They convince themselves that they will stop when they say "I do," as if it were that simple. He also warns that people often speak only about **premarital chastity**, as if chastity in marriage were not needed. Some did not engage in what they shouldn't have before marriage, and in marriage they continue with "all sorts of disgusting things" with the excuse that they had an argument or that it doesn't bother anyone if no one knows.

Daniel also shares a personal testimony. He started flipping through the first pornographic magazines at **10 or 11 years old**, and he got married at **24**. He was exposed to such content for much longer than he had access to the marital bed in the first week of marriage. Therefore, it is not realistic to expect that motivation and attitudes will overcome long-term **slavery to addiction** overnight. That must be taken seriously.

**Project 41**

Kruno states that today there are more and more programs for getting out of that addiction. His association recently launched **Project 41**, based on Sacred Scripture and prayer, intended primarily for Catholic men. Men from 20 to 60 years old come to him, in a relationship or married. Some already have grandchildren, yet they watch pornographic content with girls the age of their granddaughters and cannot stop. Kruno concludes that this is a great battle. All tools can be offered, but there is no help until a man himself says: **"Enough!"** Daniel agrees.

sections.subtitle: Čuvali su se do braka, ali to nije vještina: razočaranja u bračnoj postelji
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel objašnjava seksualnu kompatibilnost kao vještinu koja se uči
sections.content:
Kruno otvara osjetljivu temu. Što savjetovati onima koji nisu imali spolne odnose, nisu bili izloženi pornografiji ni masturbaciji, a u braku dožive razočaranje? Neki ne znaju rade li stvari ispravno ni trebaju li se tako osjećati, pa čak izbjegavaju bračnu postelju jer im je neugodna.

Daniel priznaje da je pitanje kompleksno. U Europi i Americi sve se više govori o **„sexless marriageu”**, braku bez spolnih odnosa, koji ima različite uzroke. Smatra da treba biti pošten: tko se čuvao do braka, izgradio je karakter, vrijednosti, razmišljanje o čistoći i poštovanje prema budućoj supruzi, ali **nije razvio vještinu**.

**Seksualna kompatibilnost kao komunikacija**

Daniel ističe da je **seksualna kompatibilnost također vrsta komunikacije**. Način na koji supružnici uživaju jedno u drugome vještina je koja se uči i razvija. Oni koji su bili ovisni o pornografiji to su „naučili” kroz pornografiju, pa u bračnu sobu donose mnogo prtljage o tome što bi partneru navodno trebalo biti ugodno. Oni koji su se čuvali nisu donijeli ništa. Neki su, kao nekoć i Daniel i Kate, naivno mislili da tu nema što znati jer će se sve samo dogoditi.

Takvu sliku stvaraju i **filmovi**, u kojima je sve idealno, oboje su na kraju sretni i nitko ništa ne pita. Kruno dodaje šaljivu opasku o istodobnom orgazmu. Daniel primjećuje da nitko ne objasni ni jednostavne praktične stvari, primjerice da se nakon toga ne može odmah zaspati.

**Normalno je ne znati**

Ako je već sramotno tražiti pomoć zbog loše komunikacije, kod ove teme stigma je još veća jer je mnogo privatnija. Daniel ipak naglašava da je **potpuno normalno ne znati što se radi**. Potrebna je edukacija, primjerice dobre knjige, osobito iz **kršćanske perspektive**. Takve knjige ne prodaju seksualnost niti je uzdižu u nebesa, nego je smještaju u kontekst Bogom danog dara za uživanje i rađanje djece. Spominje i Pavlovu poslanicu **Korinćanima**, prema kojoj se supružnici ne bi trebali uzdržavati kako ih Sotona ne bi zaveo. Uz šalu dodaje da nikad nije bio u napasti posvetiti se molitvi toliko da ne bi imao vremena za svoju dragu.

Daniel i Kate nisu tražili psihološku pomoć, ali su otvoreno razgovarali sa svojim **bračnim savjetnicima**. Tom iskustvu posvećeno je jedno poglavlje knjige koju su izdali, **„Naše (ne)dovršene priče”**. U njemu opisuju kako su zapeli i shvatili da ne funkcionira pristup u kojem je muž „namiren”, a žena to „odradi”. Oboje su željeli uživati jedno u drugome i morali su otkriti kako do toga doći.
sections.subtitle_en: They saved themselves until marriage, but that is not a skill: disappointments in the marital bed
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel explains sexual compatibility as a skill that is learned
sections.content_en:
Kruno opens a sensitive topic. What advice should be given to those who have not had sexual intercourse, have not been exposed to pornography or masturbation, and in marriage experience disappointment? Some do not know whether they are doing things correctly or whether they should feel that way, and even avoid the marital bed because it is uncomfortable for them.

Daniel admits that the question is complex. In Europe and America, there is more and more talk about **"sexless marriage"**, marriage without sexual intercourse, which has various causes. He believes that one should be fair: whoever saved themselves until marriage built character, values, thinking about purity, and respect toward their future wife, but **did not develop the skill**.

**Sexual compatibility as communication**

Daniel emphasizes that **sexual compatibility is also a type of communication**. The way spouses enjoy each other is a skill that is learned and developed. Those who were addicted to pornography "learned" this through pornography, so they bring a lot of baggage into the marital bedroom about what should supposedly be pleasurable for their partner. Those who saved themselves brought nothing. Some, like Daniel and Kate once did, naively thought that there was nothing to know there because everything would just happen on its own.

Such an image is also created by **movies**, in which everything is ideal, both are happy in the end, and no one asks anything. Kruno adds a humorous remark about simultaneous orgasm. Daniel notices that no one explains even simple practical things, for example that one cannot fall asleep immediately after that.

**It is normal not to know**

If it is already shameful to seek help due to poor communication, with this topic the stigma is even greater because it is much more private. Daniel nevertheless emphasizes that **it is completely normal not to know what one is doing**. Education is needed, for example good books, especially from a **Christian perspective**. Such books do not sell sexuality nor elevate it to the heavens, but rather place it in the context of a God-given gift for enjoyment and childbearing. He also mentions Paul's epistle to the **Corinthians**, according to which spouses should not abstain so that Satan would not tempt them. With a joke, he adds that he was never in temptation to dedicate himself to prayer so much that he wouldn't have time for his sweetheart.

Daniel and Kate did not seek psychological help, but they spoke openly with their **marriage counselors**. One chapter of the book they published, **„Naše (ne)dovršene priče”**, is dedicated to that experience. In it, they describe how they got stuck and realized that an approach where the husband is "satisfied" and the wife "gets it done" does not work. Both wanted to enjoy each other and had to discover how to get there.

sections.subtitle: Supružnika smo izabrali, dijete dobili: intimnost u godinama male djece
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel objašnjava zašto supružnici moraju namjerno ostati povezani kad dođu djeca
sections.content:
Daniel naglašava da se par mora uskladiti s razdobljem života u kojem se nalazi. Kad su djeca mala, majke su iscrpljene na svaki mogući način, pa se treba prilagoditi novoj situaciji.

Navodi i pitanje koje im je netko nedavno postavio: što ako beba spava u bračnom krevetu? Daniel ne želi roditeljima samo poručiti da beba ne smije spavati s njima. Svjestan je da je tako lakše, osobito kad majka noću doji. Kate je savjetovala da bebu na početku noći stave u njezin krevetić, a ako se u dva ujutro probudi za hranjenje, neka ostane s njima. Tako supružnici imaju barem dio večeri u kojem znaju da su sami.

To nije uvijek lako izvesti. Daniel se prisjeća da su živjeli u malom stanu sa samo spavaćom sobom i kuhinjom, pa je cijeli **kinderbet** doslovno nosio u kuhinju.

**Misao koja mijenja perspektivu**

Daniel ističe da je dijete dar i blagoslov od Boga, ali da su se supružnici **jedno drugo izabrali, a dijete su dobili**. S djetetom će roditelj uvijek ostati povezan jer mu je roditelj. Sa supružnikom **mora** ostati povezan jer ga je odabrao. Bez namjernih koraka zbližavanja dolazi do izolacije. On je umoran, ona je umorna, on je razočaran, ona nema volje, i tri tjedna kasnije pitaju se što im se dogodilo. Zato treba biti **namjerniji**.

**Prijatelji od povjerenja**

Puno im je pomoglo, a to je i Kate isticala, što ona ima nekoliko prijateljica s kojima može otvoreno razgovarati o izazovima braka. To su ljudi od povjerenja koji su spremni otvoreno reći da im nešto ne funkcionira, da ih boli ili da se ne znaju nositi s nekom situacijom. Ponekad pomaže već i to da se nekome sve ispriča. Ponekad treba potražiti konkretniju pomoć. Rješenje, prema Danielu, nikako nije zanemariti problem.

Brak bi trebao značiti da su supružnici **sjedinjeni na svakoj razini bića**: dušom, duhom i tijelom, ali i u ciljevima, interesima i obitelji koju podižu. Njihov je zadatak otkriti kako ostati zajedno.

**Posljedice pornografije na bračnu intimnost**

Daniel se na kraju ove teme vraća vlastitom iskustvu s posljedicama pornografije. Ona stvara dojam da su žene uvijek spremne i da nitko nikad nije razočaran. U stvarnosti se događa da ništa ne uspije ili da on bude gotov za tri minute, a nitko nije sretan. U početku se par samo ispriča, ali s vremenom shvati da o tome mora razgovarati i potražiti odgovarajuće rješenje.
sections.subtitle_en: We chose our spouse, we received our child: intimacy in the years of young children
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel explains why spouses must intentionally stay connected when children arrive
sections.content_en:
Daniel emphasizes that a couple must align with the season of life they are in. When children are young, mothers are exhausted in every possible way, so one needs to adapt to the new situation.

He also cites a question someone recently asked them: what if the baby sleeps in the marital bed? Daniel does not want to simply tell parents that the baby must not sleep with them. He is aware that it is easier that way, especially when the mother is breastfeeding at night. Kate advised putting the baby in their crib at the beginning of the night, and if they wake up at two in the morning for a feeding, let them stay with them. That way, spouses have at least a part of the evening in which they know they are alone.

That is not always easy to carry out. Daniel recalls that they lived in a small apartment with only a bedroom and a kitchen, so he literally carried the entire **crib** into the kitchen.

**A thought that changes perspective**

Daniel emphasizes that a child is a gift and a blessing from God, but that spouses **chose each other, and received the child**. A parent will always stay connected with a child because they are their parent. With a spouse, one **must** stay connected because they chose them. Without intentional steps of growing closer, isolation occurs. He is tired, she is tired, he is disappointed, she has no desire, and three weeks later they wonder what happened to them. Therefore, one needs to be **more intentional**.

**Trusted friends**

It helped them a lot, and Kate emphasized this as well, that she has several female friends with whom she can openly talk about the challenges of marriage. These are trusted people who are ready to say openly that something is not working for them, that it hurts them, or that they do not know how to handle a situation. Sometimes it helps already just to tell someone everything. Sometimes more concrete help needs to be sought. The solution, according to Daniel, is by no means to ignore the problem.

Marriage should mean that spouses are **united at every level of being**: in soul, spirit, and body, but also in goals, interests, and the family they are raising. Their task is to discover how to stay together.

**The consequences of pornography on marital intimacy**

At the end of this topic, Daniel returns to his own experience with the consequences of pornography. It creates the impression that women are always ready and that no one is ever disappointed. In reality, it happens that nothing works out or that he is done in three minutes, and no one is happy. At first, the couple merely apologizes, but over time realizes that they must talk about it and look for an appropriate solution.
