sections.subtitle: Nije problem koliko novca imate, nego kako ga trošite
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel Wurzberg objašnjava da financijski problemi u braku ne ovise o visini primanja
sections.content:
Nakon razgovora o spolnosti, voditelj **Kruno** prelazi na temu koja, kako kaže, u braku najčešće dolazi do izražaja odmah uz intimnost: **financije**. Primjećuje da muškarce možda najviše boli kada ih se udari po novčaniku, jednako kao kada ih se udari po intimnosti. Zato pita gosta kakva su iskustva iz bračnog savjetovanja.

**Daniel Wurzberg** kao prvi problem navodi lažnu uvjerenost parova da su na tom području kompatibilni. Iskustvo udruge Fokus pokazuje nešto što mnoge iznenadi: problem gotovo nikad nije u tome koliko novca par ima. *„Puno ili malo novaca, to je zapravo svejedno, uvijek je izazov kako ih trošite“*, ističe Daniel.

Objašnjava da se oba supružnika obično znaju prilagoditi oskudici. Kad par ima samo jednu plaću, pola plaće ili su oboje ostali bez posla, znaju se „stisnuti“. Problem nastaje kada su se oboje odrekli nečega, a jedan od njih sebi ipak kupi što poželi, dok drugi to nije mogao. Daniel to slikovito opisuje: oboje su bili spremni na žrtvu, a onda je jedan otišao na dvije kave, iako se kava mogla piti i kod kuće.

### Anegdota o 20.000 kuna

Kao drugu stranu iste priče Daniel navodi susret s jednim mladićem. Bilo je to još u vrijeme kuna, a mladić mu se požalio: *„Gle, ja imam 20.000 kn mjesečno, ja si ni majicu ne mogu priuštit.“* Daniel se tada zapitao kako je to moguće, jer je on sam imao pet puta manja primanja i troje djece. Zaključak je jasan: **nije problem imati novac, nego kako se njime upravlja.**
sections.subtitle_en: The problem is not how much money you have, but how you spend it
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel Wurzberg explains that financial problems in marriage do not depend on the amount of income
sections.content_en:
After the conversation about sexuality, host **Kruno** moves on to a topic that, as he says, most often comes to the fore in marriage right alongside intimacy: **finances**. He notes that it perhaps hurts men the most when they are hit in the wallet, just as when they are hit in intimacy. That is why he asks the guest what the experiences from marriage counseling are.

**Daniel Wurzberg** cites as the first problem couples' false conviction that they are compatible in that area. The experience of the association Fokus shows something that surprises many: the problem is almost never how much money a couple has. *“A lot or a little money, it is actually all the same, the challenge is always how you spend it,”* Daniel points out.

He explains that both spouses usually know how to adapt to scarcity. When a couple has only one salary, half a salary, or both have lost their jobs, they know how to “tighten up.” The problem arises when both have given up something, and one of them still buys whatever they want for themselves, while the other could not. Daniel vividly describes it: both were ready for sacrifice, and then one went out for two coffees, even though coffee could have been drunk at home.

### Anecdote about 20,000 kuna

As the other side of the same story, Daniel cites an encounter with a young man. It was still back in the time of the kuna, and the young man complained to him: *“Look, I have 20,000 kn a month, I can't even afford a T-shirt for myself.”* Daniel then wondered how that was possible, because he himself had five times lower income and three children. The conclusion is clear: **the problem is not having money, but how it is managed.**

sections.subtitle: Lekcija o novcu tek nakon medenog mjeseca
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o vrijednostima iz roditeljskog doma i o tome zašto se lekcija o financijama ostavlja za kraj tečaja
sections.content:
Prema Danielu, veliku ulogu u odnosu prema novcu imaju **vrijednosti koje supružnici donose iz svojih obitelji**. Važno je kako su njihovi roditelji upravljali financijama, tko je za to bio odgovoran te jesu li se stalno mučili da spoje kraj s krajem ili su novcem upravljali mudro. Mnogo toga ovisi o tome kakav se par nađe, no o financijama se u svakom slučaju mora razgovarati.

Daniel to smatra jednom od važnijih lekcija. Zato u udruzi u posljednje vrijeme na zaručničkim tečajevima **lekciju o financijama ostavljaju za razdoblje nakon medenog mjeseca**. Objašnjava razlog: na medenom mjesecu mladenci se obično dobro počaste, s osjećajem da si mogu priuštiti što god žele. Onda ih udari svakodnevica u kojoj idu na posao i žive od plaće do plaće.

Tek se tada, kaže Daniel, jasnije vidi s kakvim vrijednostima supružnici pristupaju vođenju kućnog budžeta. Kruno dodaje da se do tada „skupi materijala“, a Daniel se slaže.
sections.subtitle_en: A lesson about money only after the honeymoon
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about values from the parental home and about why the lesson on finances is left for the end of the course
sections.content_en:
According to Daniel, a major role in the attitude toward money is played by the **values that spouses bring from their families**. It matters how their parents managed finances, who was responsible for it, and whether they constantly struggled to make ends meet or managed money wisely. Much depends on what kind of couple comes together, but finances must be discussed in any case.

Daniel considers this one of the more important lessons. That is why in the association lately, in marriage preparation courses, **they leave the lesson on finances for the period after the honeymoon**. He explains the reason: on the honeymoon, newlyweds usually treat themselves well, with the feeling that they can afford whatever they want. Then everyday life hits them, in which they go to work and live from paycheck to paycheck.

Only then, Daniel says, is it seen more clearly with what values the spouses approach managing the household budget. Kruno adds that by then "material has gathered," and Daniel agrees.

sections.subtitle: Kad novac postane oruđe manipulacije
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel Wurzberg opisuje slučaj para u kojem je posuđeni novac narušio povjerenje
sections.content:
Daniel naglašava da razočaranja i prve svađe oko novca nisu nepremostive, ali da se **povjerenje mora graditi**. Kao primjer navodi par u kojem je muž posudio novac od roditelja svoje supruge. Novac nije iskoristio za ono što je obećao, nego je negdje nestao. Daniel ne zna je li ga prokockao ili je bilo nešto slično.

Potrošeni novac pritom nije bio glavni problem. Muž je taj iznos mogao zaraditi i vratiti kroz nekoliko mjeseci. Glavni problem bilo je **narušeno povjerenje**. Rečenica više nije glasila *„Dužan si mojim roditeljima“*, nego *„Ne mogu ti vjerovati“*. Daniel ističe razliku: da se mužu razbio auto pa je par završio u minusu, to bi bila jedna priča. Ovdje je, međutim, riječ o iskorištenom povjerenju i pitanju kako dalje.

Njegov zaključak je ozbiljan. Ako par primijeti da novcem pokušava **manipulirati jedno drugim**, da potajno nešto kupuje ili skriva, tada ima mnogo dublji problem kojim se mora pozabaviti.
sections.subtitle_en: When money becomes a tool of manipulation
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel Wurzberg describes the case of a couple in which borrowed money damaged trust
sections.content_en:
Daniel emphasizes that disappointments and first arguments over money are not insurmountable, but that **trust must be built**. As an example, he cites a couple where the husband borrowed money from his wife's parents. He did not use the money for what he had promised, but rather it disappeared somewhere. Daniel does not know whether he gambled it away or if it was something similar.

The spent money was not the main problem here. The husband could have earned that amount and repaid it over a few months. The main problem was **damaged trust**. The sentence was no longer *"You owe my parents"*, but *"I cannot trust you"*. Daniel highlights the difference: if the husband's car had been totaled and the couple ended up in the red, that would be one story. Here, however, it is a matter of exploited trust and the question of how to move forward.

His conclusion is serious. If a couple notices that they are trying to **manipulate each other** with money, secretly buying something or hiding it, then they have a much deeper problem that must be addressed.

sections.subtitle: „Naše (ne)dovršene priče“: razvodi koji se nisu dogodili
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj predstavlja knjigu „Naše nedovršene priče – Razvodi koji se nisu dogodili“
sections.content:
Kruno zatim predstavlja knjigu **„Naše nedovršene priče – Razvodi koji se nisu dogodili“**. Naziva je sjajnom knjigom punom svjedočanstava i plodom rada udruge. Ističe da je poticajno čitati priče parova koji su došli gotovo do ruba, a ipak su uspjeli nadići krizu. Svaki čitatelj, smatra, može se prepoznati u nekom od svjedočanstava. Zato pita gosta koja je priča njemu osobno progovorila.

Daniel odgovara da na njega nisu najveći dojam ostavile same priče, nego **proces kroz koji su autori prošli dok su ih pisali**. Pojašnjava i naslov. Knjiga se ne zove „Razvodi koji se nisu dogodili“ zato što su svi parovi nužno bili pred razvodom. Neke priče govore o svakodnevnom trenju, na primjer o paru u kojem je on ekstrovert, a ona introvert, pa se oko toga stalno natežu. To nije razlog za razvod, ali je stalan izvor napetosti.

Zanimljivo je da je Daniel ranije u razgovoru otkrio kako jedno poglavlje knjige govori i o njegovu braku s Kate. U njemu opisuju razdoblje u kojem su na području intime „zapeli“ i potražili pomoć bračnih savjetnika.
entities: Naše nedovršene priče – Razvodi koji se nisu dogodili
sections.subtitle_en: "Our (Un)finished Stories": Divorces That Did Not Happen
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host presents the book "Our Unfinished Stories – Divorces That Did Not Happen"
sections.content_en:
Kruno then presents the book **"Our Unfinished Stories – Divorces That Did Not Happen"**. He calls it a great book full of testimonies and the fruit of the association's work. He emphasizes that it is encouraging to read the stories of couples who came almost to the brink, and yet managed to overcome the crisis. Every reader, he believes, can recognize themselves in one of the testimonies. That is why he asks the guest which story spoke to him personally.

Daniel replies that the greatest impression was not left on him by the stories themselves, but by **the process the authors went through while writing them**. He also clarifies the title. The book is not called "Divorces That Did Not Happen" because all the couples were necessarily on the verge of divorce. Some stories speak of everyday friction, for example about a couple where he is an extrovert and she is an introvert, so they constantly bicker over that. That is not a reason for divorce, but it is a constant source of tension.

Interestingly, Daniel earlier in the conversation revealed that one chapter of the book also speaks about his marriage with Kate. In it, they describe a period in which they got "stuck" in the area of intimacy and sought the help of marriage counselors.
entities_en: Our Unfinished Stories – Divorces That Did Not Happen

sections.subtitle: Pisanje kao terapija: priča o tri spontana pobačaja
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel Wurzberg prepričava svjedočanstvo para koji je prošao kroz tri spontana pobačaja
sections.content:
Urednici knjige postavili su autorima dva ključna uvjeta:

- **Oba supružnika moraju napisati svoju perspektivu.** Nije bilo dovoljno da, primjerice, samo žena hrabro opiše kako je bilo.
- **Pišu iz perspektive razdoblja kroz koje su prolazili**, a ne samo iz današnje, smirenije pozicije.

Rezultat je iznenadio i same urednike. Neki su parovi priznali da im je pisanje bilo **kao terapija**. Jedna supruga rekla je da zapravo nikad nije čula kako se njezin muž nosio s onim kroz što su prošli zajedno.

Daniel posebno izdvaja priču para koji je doživio **tri spontana pobačaja**. Objašnjava da se spontani pobačaj može dogoditi u svakoj trudnoći. Nakon prvoga par se tješi da će ih Bog iscijeliti i da će pokušati ponovno. Nakon trećega, međutim, javljaju se teška pitanja: je li kriv on, je li kriva ona, što ne valja. Muž je u knjizi napisao da prvi pobačaj nije doživio teško jer su znali da se može dogoditi. No kada je nakon trećega morao ići u bolnicu, to je doživio sasvim drugačije. Supruga je tek tada čula kako se on s tim nosio.

Daniel zaključuje da je prilika da ispričaju svoju priču parovima dala više od platforme. Omogućila im je da **procesuiraju bol** kroz koju su prošli. Neki od njih u braku su već po 30 godina, a tek su sada otkrili dio svog odnosa koji nikad nisu izrekli riječima. Bog ih je vjerno nosio kroz to razdoblje, ali tek su sada mogli reći: *„Nisam znala da si se tako osjećao, da te to toliko boljelo.“* Za Daniela je to najdublji dojam: da su se supružnici vidjeli i čuli na novi način.
sections.subtitle_en: Writing as therapy: the story of three miscarriages
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel Wurzberg recounts the testimony of a couple who went through three miscarriages
sections.content_en:
The editors of the book set two key conditions for the authors:

- **Both spouses must write their perspective.** It was not enough for, for example, only the wife to bravely describe what it was like.
- **They write from the perspective of the period they were going through**, and not just from today's, calmer position.

The result surprised even the editors themselves. Some couples admitted that writing was **like therapy** for them. One wife said that she had actually never heard how her husband coped with what they went through together.

Daniel particularly singles out the story of a couple who experienced **three miscarriages**. He explains that a miscarriage can happen in any pregnancy. After the first one, the couple consoles themselves that God will heal them and that they will try again. After the third, however, difficult questions arise: is it his fault, is it her fault, what is wrong. The husband wrote in the book that he did not take the first miscarriage hard because they knew it could happen. But when he had to go to the hospital after the third, he experienced it completely differently. Only then did the wife hear how he coped with it.

Daniel concludes that the opportunity to tell their story gave the couples more than a platform. It enabled them to **process the pain** they went through. Some of them have been married for as long as 30 years, and only now have they discovered a part of their relationship that they had never put into words. God faithfully carried them through that period, but only now could they say: *„I didn't know that you felt that way, that it hurt you so much.“* For Daniel, that is the deepest impression: that the spouses saw and heard each other in a new way.

sections.subtitle: Male grupe i brak koji živi misijski
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o pitanjima za promišljanje i važnosti malih grupa za bračne parove
sections.content:
Pisanje nije pomoglo samo autorima, nego obogaćuje i čitatelje. Daniel priznaje da se ne može svatko poistovjetiti sa svakom pričom. Jedna od njih, primjerice, govori o **bankrotu**. Ipak, svi znaju kako je imati ili nemati novac i boriti se da se plate računi, pa se i s takvom pričom čitatelj može povezati.

Svaka priča završava **s nekoliko pitanja za promišljanje**. Daniel ističe da je upravo to cijela ideja knjige. Ona nije samo zbirka svjedočanstava, nego bi trebala potaknuti razgovor, posebno u maloj grupi. U Fokusu su, kaže, *„strastveno uvjereni“* da je **mala grupa plodno tlo za svaki brak**. U njoj parovi uče na primjeru drugih i prije svega otkrivaju da nisu sami i da nisu ludi.

Daniel nabraja s čime se parovi bore:

- s problemima u bračnoj postelji,
- s financijama,
- s odgojem djece,
- s nemogućnošću da imaju djecu, što je tema jedne od priča u knjizi.

Kad par otkrije krug ljudi s kojima može rasti i dijeliti vrijednosti, lakše ide dalje. Daniel se nada da Bog takve priče može iskoristiti i da ohrabri ljude koje autori nikad neće sresti uživo. Takvi čitatelji možda će se zapitati kako ono kroz što su sami prošli može biti Bogu na slavu.

Krajnji je cilj potaknuti parove da otkriju kako se **brak može živjeti na misijski način**. Brak ne postoji samo radi dvoje supružnika, nego i radi društva u kojem žive. Može biti svjedočanstvo djeci, roditeljima, rodbini, a zatim i mnogo širem krugu ljudi.
sections.subtitle_en: Small groups and a marriage that lives missionally
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about reflection questions and the importance of small groups for married couples
sections.content_en:
Writing did not only help the authors, but also enriches the readers. Daniel admits that not everyone can identify with every story. One of them, for example, speaks about **bankruptcy**. Still, everyone knows what it is like to have or not have money and struggle to pay the bills, so a reader can connect even with such a story.

Every story ends **with several reflection questions**. Daniel emphasizes that this is precisely the whole idea of the book. It is not just a collection of testimonies, but should encourage conversation, especially in a small group. In Fokus, he says, they are *„passionately convinced“* that a **small group is fertile ground for every marriage**. In it, couples learn from the example of others and, above all, discover that they are not alone and that they are not crazy.

Daniel lists what couples struggle with:

- with problems in the marital bed,
- with finances,
- with raising children,
- with the inability to have children, which is the theme of one of the stories in the book.

When a couple discovers a circle of people with whom they can grow and share values, it is easier to move forward. Daniel hopes that God can use such stories to encourage people whom the authors will never meet in person. Such readers may wonder how what they themselves have gone through can be for God's glory.

The ultimate goal is to encourage couples to discover how **marriage can be lived in a missional way**. Marriage does not exist only for the sake of the two spouses, but also for the sake of the society in which they live. It can be a testimony to children, parents, relatives, and then to a much wider circle of people.

sections.subtitle: Od Tjedna braka do serijala „Budi odvažan“
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel Wurzberg predstavlja program „Budi odvažan“, video serijal od deset lekcija za muškarce
sections.content:
Kruno priznaje da mu je epizoda proletjela i da bi se o knjizi moglo govoriti mnogo duže. Prije kraja izdvaja još neke projekte udruge Fokus:

- **Nacionalni tjedan braka**, koji se održava tjedan dana prije Valentinova,
- **Vikende za pamćenje**, okupljanja na određenoj lokaciji namijenjena samo bračnim parovima, najčešće bez djece, što voditelj smatra velikim plusom.

Zatim pita kako udruga pristupa muškarcima i postoji li program posvećen samo njima.

Daniel potvrđuje da postoji. Riječ je o programu **„Budi odvažan“**, video serijalu od **deset lekcija** koji obrađuje teme s kojima se bori većina muškaraca. Među njima su:

- pitanje vlastitog identiteta,
- različite ovisnosti,
- pornografija, o kojoj se u razgovoru već govorilo.

Serijal želi pokazati muškarcu da može učiniti mnogo više za zajednicu u kojoj živi. To uključuje odgovornost onoga koji se brine za svoj dom, dobro ljubljenje vlastite supruge i uključivanje u živote drugih muškaraca. Daniel opisuje i dvostruku ulogu mentorstva. S jedne strane muškarac treba **imati mentora**, nekoga starijeg i zrelijeg tko će govoriti u njegov život. S druge strane i sam treba **postati mentor** mlađima i otkriti da može nešto dati ako za to odvoji vrijeme i bude namjeran.
sections.subtitle_en: From Marriage Week to the "Budi odvažan" series
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel Wurzberg presents the program "Budi odvažan", a ten-lesson video series for men
sections.content_en:
Kruno admits that the episode flew by for him and that one could talk about the book for much longer. Before the end, he highlights a few more projects of the Fokus association:

- **National Marriage Week**, which is held a week before Valentine's Day,
- **Weekends to Remember**, gatherings at a specific location intended only for married couples, most often without children, which the host considers a great plus.

Then he asks how the association approaches men and whether there is a program dedicated only to them.

Daniel confirms that there is. It is the program **"Budi odvažan"**, a video series of **ten lessons** that addresses topics that most men struggle with. Among them are:

- the question of one's own identity,
- various addictions,
- pornography, which was already discussed in the conversation.

The series wants to show a man that he can do much more for the community in which he lives. That includes the responsibility of the one who cares for his home, loving his wife well, and being involved in the lives of other men. Daniel also describes the twofold role of mentorship. On the one hand, a man needs to **have a mentor**, someone older and more mature who will speak into his life. On the other hand, he himself needs to **become a mentor** to younger ones and discover that he can give something if he sets aside time for it and is intentional.

sections.subtitle: Kobasice na vatri i vjera koja ne staje nedjeljom
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje „Budi odvažan“ vikend u Gorskom kotaru
sections.content:
Program se provodi svaka dva tjedna, pa deset susreta traje nekoliko mjeseci. Daniel je, međutim, svjestan da muškarci neće samo sjediti oko stola i razgovarati o onome što je dobro za njihov život. Zato se jednom godišnje održava **„Budi odvažan“ vikend u Gorskom kotaru**. Tamo sudionici peku kobasice na vatri i planinare, ali i promišljaju kako izgleda vjera u životu pobožnog muškarca.

Pitanja koja si postavljaju vrlo su konkretna: kako vjera izgleda na poslu, kako u obitelji, a kako u životu studenta i njegovu svjedočanstvu ondje gdje se nalazi. Cilj je, ističe Daniel, da se vjera ne svede na nešto što se događa nedjeljom, dok muškarac od ponedjeljka do subote živi kako zna, a onda je opet malo pobožan.

Vikend u šumi oduševljava muškarce. Upoznaju sebe i druge, a posebno oni koji dolaze iz grada otkrivaju da ipak postoje ljudi s kojima mogu podijeliti takve stvari i koji ih razumiju.

Daniel ipak naglašava da jedan vikend neće nikome promijeniti cijelu godinu ako nakon toga ne ulaže u područja koja je otkrio. Navodi primjere: netko se cijeli život smatra vjernikom, a shvati da nikad sam nije pročitao Bibliju. Drugi dobro zarađuje za obitelj, ali uvidi da kod kuće ima djecu koja ga trebaju, a on za njih nema vremena upravo zato što radi. Takav bi, sugerira Daniel, mogao sljedeći put na vikend povesti sina ili mu se na neki drugi način približiti.
sections.subtitle_en: Sausages over the fire and a faith that does not stop on Sunday
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes the "Budi odvažan" weekend in Gorski kotar
sections.content_en:
The program is carried out every two weeks, so ten meetings last several months. Daniel is, however, aware that men will not just sit around a table and talk about what is good for their lives. That is why once a year a **"Budi odvažan" weekend in Gorski kotar** is held. There, participants roast sausages over the fire and hike, but also reflect on what faith looks like in the life of a devout man.

The questions they ask themselves are very concrete: what faith looks like at work, what it looks like in the family, and what it looks like in the life of a student and his witness where he finds himself. The goal is, Daniel points out, that faith is not reduced to something that happens on Sunday, while from Monday to Saturday a man lives as best he can, and then is a little devout again.

The weekend in the forest thrills the men. They get to know themselves and others, and especially those who come from the city discover that there are indeed people with whom they can share such things and who understand them.

Daniel nevertheless emphasizes that one weekend will not change the entire year for anyone if after that he does not invest in the areas he has discovered. He cites examples: someone has considered himself a believer his whole life, yet realizes that he has never read the Bible on his own. Another earns well for the family, but sees that at home he has children who need him, while he has no time for them precisely because he works. Such a person, Daniel suggests, could next time bring his son along to the weekend or draw closer to him in some other way.

sections.subtitle: Zašto jedan vikend nije dovoljan
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel Wurzberg prepričava razgovor sa sudionikom kojeg je nakon vikenda hvatala depresija
sections.content:
Daniel ističe da su važni i program s kontinuitetom, poput serijala koji traje tri mjeseca, i vikend koji za mnoge bude tek početak promišljanja. Na vikend ponekad dođu muškarci koji su događaj vidjeli na društvenim mrežama. Stignu *„k'o padobranci“*, bez ikakvih očekivanja, a onda se iznenade koliko im je nešto takvo nedostajalo.

Ispričao je i anegdotu sa sudionikom kojeg je prošle godine pitao hoće li opet doći. Muškarac mu je odgovorio da više neće. Vikend mu je bio jedan od najboljih u životu, ali nakon njega upao je u tešku depresiju jer se kod kuće ništa nije promijenilo. Daniel mu je odgovorio da je to zato što živi od vikenda do vikenda, a cijelu godinu između ne poduzima ništa. Kruno dodaje: *„Ne radiš na sebi.“*

Daniel u tome vidi **boljku muškaraca**: spremni su brzo zasukati rukave, ali im nedostaje ustrajnosti. Malo će se toga dogoditi preko noći, za jedan vikend ili tjedan predavanja. Uspoređuje to s treningom: *„Tko god je vježbao zna da u tjedan dana možeš samo pare potrošit.“* Uspjeh dolazi tek s dosljednošću. Tada čovjek otkriva čega se mora riješiti, u što mora uložiti i čemu se želi posvetiti.

Zato je potreban **ekosustav podrške**. To može biti, na primjer, WhatsApp grupa s trojicom prijatelja koji hrabre muškarca da ustraje. Takvo okruženje hrani njegovu odluku za bolje i pomaže mu da nastavi živjeti u skladu s njom. Kruno to sažima izrekom: *„S kim si, takav si.“*
sections.subtitle_en: Why one weekend is not enough
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel Wurzberg recounts a conversation with a participant who was gripped by depression after the weekend
sections.content_en:
Daniel points out that both a program with continuity, like a series that lasts three months, and a weekend that for many is only the beginning of reflection, are important. Men who saw the event on social media sometimes come to the weekend. They arrive *“like paratroopers”*, without any expectations, and then they are surprised by how much they missed something like that.

He also shared an anecdote about a participant whom he asked last year whether he would come again. The man answered him that he would not anymore. The weekend was one of the best in his life for him, but after it he fell into a severe depression because nothing had changed at home. Daniel replied to him that this is because he lives from weekend to weekend, and during the entire year in between he does not do anything. Kruno adds: *“You are not working on yourself.”*

Daniel sees in this a **men's ailment**: they are ready to quickly roll up their sleeves, but they lack perseverance. Little of it will happen overnight, in one weekend or a week of lectures. He compares this to training: *“Whoever has worked out knows that in a week you can only spend money.”* Success comes only with consistency. Then a man discovers what he must get rid of, what he must invest in, and what he wants to dedicate himself to.

That is why a **support ecosystem** is needed. That can be, for example, a WhatsApp group with three friends who encourage the man to persevere. Such an environment feeds his decision for the better and helps him continue living in accordance with it. Kruno summarizes this with the saying: *“You are who you are with.”*

sections.subtitle: Redefinicija: brak i emocionalno zreo muškarac
sections.screenshot_description: Gost razmišlja o definiciji braka u blic pitanjima „Redefinicija“
sections.content:
Na kraju Kruno uvodi blic pitanja pod nazivom **„Redefinicija“**, u kojima od gosta traži definicije pojmova u jednoj rečenici.

**Kako bi definirao brak?** Daniel kratko razmisli, a zatim odgovori:

> *„Savez dvoje dobronamjernih ljudi koji žele stavit ovo drugo ispred.“*

Kruno odgovor prihvaća riječima: *„Stavit ćemo u rječnik.“*

**Što znači biti emocionalno zreo muškarac?** Daniel priznaje da bi se borio s tom definicijom i da je to tema koju i sam istražuje i o kojoj čita. Ističe da je ta zrelost povezana s poznavanjem sebe i spoznajom kako ga je Bog stvorio. Takav muškarac mora živjeti u skladu s onim kako je Bog zamislio život muškarca, uz pomoć Njegove riječi. Na kraju sažima: emocionalno zreo muškarac je **osoba koja se zna zrelo nositi sa situacijom**. To se odnosi na rješavanje sukoba i na preuzimanje odgovornosti za sebe, za svoje zdravlje, obitelj i djecu. Riječ je, kaže, o *„zrelosti koja preuzima odgovornost“*. Kruno odgovor ocjenjuje kao „savršen“.
sections.subtitle_en: Redefinition: Marriage and the Emotionally Mature Man
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest reflects on the definition of marriage during the "Redefinition" rapid-fire questions
sections.content_en:
At the end, Kruno introduces rapid-fire questions called **"Redefinition"**, in which he asks the guest for definitions of concepts in one sentence.

**How would you define marriage?** Daniel thinks briefly, and then replies:

> *"A covenant of two well-intentioned people who want to put the other first."*

Kruno accepts the answer with the words: *"We'll put it in the dictionary."*

**What does it mean to be an emotionally mature man?** Daniel admits that he would struggle with that definition and that it is a topic he himself explores and reads about. He emphasizes that this maturity is connected with self-knowledge and the realization of how God created him. Such a man must live in accordance with how God envisioned a man's life, with the help of His word. In the end, he summarizes: an emotionally mature man is **a person who knows how to deal with a situation maturely**. This refers to resolving conflicts and taking responsibility for oneself, for one's health, family, and children. It is about, he says, *"maturity that takes responsibility"*. Kruno evaluates the answer as "perfect".

sections.subtitle: Izazov za gledatelje: umjesto kritike ponudite rješenje
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel Wurzberg poziva gledatelje da uz svaku zamjerku ponude konkretno rješenje
sections.content:
Posljednje pitanje odnosi se na izazov koji bi gost uputio gledateljima, i muškarcima i ženama, za sljedeći tjedan u njihovoj vezi ili braku.

Daniel predlaže sljedeće. Ako u odnosu postoji nešto što partnere jako žulja, bilo da je novijeg datuma ili traje dugo, neka odvoje vrijeme da smisle **kreativan način na koji bi to riješili**. Tako iritacija ne bi postala *„samo hrana za kritiku“*, nego bi donijela rješenje.

Njegova je poruka jednostavna: **ako imaš nešto za prigovoriti, ponudi i rješenje**. Ono ne mora biti ispravno, ali osoba tada dolazi za stol s porukom: *„Želim raditi na našem odnosu, ovo me smetalo, evo jedne moje ideje.“* Daniel vjeruje da to otvara vrata napretku. Suprotan pristup sažima rečenicom: *„Meni ovo ide na živce, a ti si kriv.“*

Kruno zaključuje da treba biti konkretan i namjeran te sam preuzeti inicijativu.
sections.subtitle_en: A challenge for viewers: offer a solution instead of criticism
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel Wurzberg invites viewers to offer a concrete solution alongside every objection
sections.content_en:
The last question relates to a challenge that the guest would address to the viewers, both men and women, for the next week in their relationship or marriage.

Daniel suggests the following. If there is something in the relationship that really bothers the partners, whether it is of recent date or has been going on for a long time, let them set aside time to come up with a **creative way in which they would resolve it**. That way, the irritation would not become *„just food for criticism“*, but would bring about a solution.

His message is simple: **if you have something to complain about, offer a solution as well**. It does not have to be correct, but the person then comes to the table with the message: *„I want to work on our relationship, this bothered me, here is an idea of mine.“* Daniel believes that this opens the door to progress. He summarizes the opposite approach with the sentence: *„This gets on my nerves, and you are to blame.“*

Kruno concludes that one needs to be concrete and intentional, and take the initiative oneself.

sections.subtitle: Za deset godina? „U Božjoj milosti, kao i do sad“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost odgovara na posljednje pitanje gdje se vidi za deset godina
sections.content:
Kruno zahvaljuje Danielu što je *„probio led“* u prvoj epizodi podcasta i izražava nadu da će se opet susresti. Gledatelje poziva na dijeljenje, lajkanje i pretplatu, *„kako se to lijepo kaže na starohrvatskom“*, te najavljuje sljedeću Redefiniciju za mjesec dana. Dodaje da članovi **Patreon** kanala već danas mogu pogledati drugu epizodu podcasta.

Nakon odjave slijedi još jedno pitanje: **gdje se gost vidi za deset godina?**

Daniel odgovara mirno: *„U Božjoj milosti, kao i do sad.“* Kaže da i dalje planira biti voljeni sin kojeg će Bog uvijek *„primiti za kragnu“* i staviti na pravo mjesto u pravo vrijeme. Zaključuje: *„To je sve što mi u životu treba. Sve drugo može otići.“*
sections.subtitle_en: In ten years? "In God's grace, as until now"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest answers the final question where he sees himself in ten years
sections.content_en:
Kruno thanks Daniel for having *"broken the ice"* in the first episode of the podcast and expresses hope that they will meet again. He invites viewers to share, like, and subscribe, *"as they nicely say in Old Croatian"*, and announces the next Redefinicija in a month. He adds that members of the **Patreon** channel can already watch the second episode of the podcast today.

After the sign-off, another question follows: **where does the guest see himself in ten years?**

Daniel answers calmly: *"In God's grace, as until now."* He says that he still plans to be a beloved son whom God will always *"grab by the collar"* and put in the right place at the right time. He concludes: *"That is all I need in life. Everything else can go."*
